questions.q:
*(Refer to the comprehension passage in Question 11)*

What was the main outcome of the 1976 voyage of the *Hōkūleʻa* as interpreted by the text?
options: It proved that skeptics were correct to call ancient wayfinding serendipitous.
It discredited the belief that indigenous Pacific navigation was merely based on luck.
It introduced modern digital GPS tracking to traditional Hawaiian canoe building.
It resulted in Dr. Silas Vance being stranded on an unseen landmass.
questions.explain: The text states that skeptics thought these feats were 'mere serendipity' (luck), but the Hōkūleʻa's voyage 'irrevocably dismantled this condescending view' and proved the 'empirical validity of indigenous knowledge.'

questions.q:
*(Refer to the comprehension passage in Question 31)*

From the instructions on terrace construction, what can be logically inferred about the function of the **gravel**?
options: It acts as a primary fertilizer for the crops being planted.
It provides a porous layer that prevents water from getting trapped and breaking the wall.
It is used exclusively to cement the stones of the retaining wall together.
It stops the flow of water entirely so the soil stays dry.
questions.explain: The text states the space behind the wall is 'backfilled with gravel for drainage'. Since the goal is to move water 'without breaking the stone walls,' it can be inferred that the gravel allows water to flow safely through (drainage) rather than building up pressure.
